title: introduce-credential-primers-retry-matrix-and-stream-concierge-cross-sdk-bump
author: Evelyn Park
release_notes: Small ergonomic API changes and bug fixes across Python/TS/Go SDKs: credential primer pre-warming, unified retry matrix, stream hints API, and patch version bumps (py 0.22.1, ts 1.14.0, go v1.8.3). No user-facing contract changes expected; backward compatible aliases provided.
description:
Motivation: In production customers reported cold-auth latency spikes and inconsistent retry behavior when a transient auth provider hiccup coincided with high-concurrency streaming workloads. This PR introduces three coordinated items across SDKs: (1) credential primers — a light-weight, configurable prefetch that warms credentials before first stream/poll, (2) a documented and enforced retry-matrix that harmonizes backoff ceilings and retriable predicate semantics across Python/TypeScript/Go, and (3) stream-concierge hints: non-breaking helpers on stream handles that allow consumers to indicate expected message cadence, aiding internal batching and prefetch heuristics.

What changed (high level): consolidated auth prefetch logic into a small shared policy, added per-SDK adapter layers to apply the primer without requiring application changes, defined a retry-matrix table and implemented it in each SDK's retry middleware, and added a lightweight StreamHints object (with ergonomic defaults) plus helper decorators to the three SDKs. Also includes docs, integration tests, and minor version bumps on package manifests.

Compatibility and ergonomics: All changes are opt-in by default. The credential primer is disabled unless an explicit small config block is supplied or the "enable_cred_primer" feature flag is set in SDK config. StreamHints are additive — existing stream APIs continue to work and receive no-op defaults. For parity, several older helper names that conflicted across SDKs were kept as deprecated aliases with console warnings to ease migration.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests added for primer edge-cases (race on first request), retry-matrix convergence tests that simulate auth-then-network failures, and language-specific stream e2e suites. Staged rollout: feature gated behind SDK config; documented upgrade guidance and recommended backoff presets for high-concurrency customers.

Related: ENG-3032 (credential stability), ENG-3058 (streaming reliability).
